players.product: Helios trapped-ion quantum computer (Quantum Charge-Coupled Device architecture)

quarterly_data.signal: Customer RIKEN: one of Quantinuum's largest customers, RIKEN accounted for 60% of revenue in fiscal 2025 and 63% in fiscal 2024 (7% in the three months to March 31, 2026 versus 90% a year earlier).

Quantinuum (prospectus): operates four commercial quantum computing systems - three at its Colorado campus and one on the RIKEN campus in Japan - with a fifth expected to be deployed in Singapore in late 2026; its Helios system achieved 48 logical qubits from only 98 physical qubits.

Quantinuum (prospectus): relies on single-source suppliers for certain advanced sensors, trap fabrication services, high-performance electronic interface products, acousto-optic devices, fiber optic cable assemblies, cryogenic components, optical and photonics components, laser systems, enriched isotope materials, electromagnetic simulation software and certain embedded-computing design and manufacturing services.

Licensor Leonardo DRS: Quantinuum's quantum computing technology depends on its license agreement with Leonardo DRS, Inc. (commenced December 11, 2025, perpetual unless terminated), a field-exclusive, worldwide licence of patents, know-how and other intellectual property to develop, manufacture and commercialize products in licensed fields that include ion-trap quantum computing.

Customer JPMorgan Chase: named (financial services) among the market leaders in Quantinuum's active customer engagements that serve as both a customer and an innovation partner; Quantinuum says it is deeply engaged with JPMorgan Chase to create new applications.

Quantinuum (prospectus): innovates on its quantum computing platform working collaboratively with partners like NVIDIA and Infineon, and its software is compatible with platforms such as NVIDIA CUDA-Q.

connects_to.relationship: Quantinuum quantum computing services distributed through Azure Quantum

contracts.signal: Quantinuum (prospectus): offers access to its quantum computing services directly through its own quantum cloud and indirectly through public cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure, which integrate its services into their own quantum computing platforms; a majority of its cloud-based business currently runs through its own cloud.

contracts.signal: Quantinuum (prospectus): in March 2026 the 2021 Strategic Services and Supply Agreement with Honeywell was terminated and Quantinuum entered a Strategic Services and Supply Agreement with Honeywell Aerospace Inc. (AERO) for goods, services and deliverables related to the fabrication of ion traps - ten-year term with automatic five-year renewals, reimbursement of labor and materials plus a 15% markup under agreed statements of work and purchase orders, no minimum purchase obligation; Quantinuum incurred $1.6 million of fabrication costs in the three months to March 31, 2026 ($1.4 million a year earlier) and made a $9.4 million prepayment to AERO for the procurement of updated equipment, with $6.3 million more to be prepaid during the rest of 2026.
contracts.value: $9.4 million equipment prepayment (+$6.3 million more in 2026); $1.6 million fabrication costs in Q1 2026

players.product: quantum system contract development and manufacturing: control systems, dilution refrigerators and flexible cables (Rigetti); planned outsourced production partner for Quantinuum systems

connects_to.relationship: planned outsourced production of Quantinuum quantum systems - the prospectus names 'partners such as Quanta' for production after in-house assembly of each generation's early systems (a stated plan)

contracts.signal: Quantinuum (prospectus): aims to scale manufacturing through a hybrid model, assembling and validating the early systems of each generation in-house before transitioning to outsourced production through partners such as Quanta, while retaining direct control over critical integration, testing and performance validation (a stated plan; no agreement or order is disclosed).
